newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand yields close lower across curve.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand yields close lower across curve.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD
OVERNIGHT CASH 7.55 PCT (PREV 7.60) US 5-YR 6.31 (PREV 6.30)
* Yields end lower in flow-driven market
* Peters', Bolger's comments seen relatively supportive
* Flows generally light
New Zealand yields on Tuesday closed easier across the curve with the move more pronounced in the short end.
Prices were initially marked down in response to a fall in Australian rates and moved little from that early move.
The 90-day banks ended at 7.36 percent against 7.44 percent at Monday's close. The bills are at their lowest for 27 months and a number of players are tipping they will breach 7.0 percent soon.
Comments of concern about the high New Zealand dollar by Treasurer Winston Peters and Prime Minister Jim Bolger, if anything helped push yields lower.
Dealers said the comments showed politicians were powerless to drive the currency down. They said that as long as the currency held its strength, bank bills would trend lower.
The market at present is flow driven though and flows were light and expected to remain that way for some time.
However, interest may perk up on Thusday when September quarter GDP data is due to be released and Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash speaks to the Canterbury Employers' Chamber of Commerce.
GPD is picked to to rise a seasonally adjusted 0.2 percent in the September quarter for an actual rise of 2.25 percent in the year.
The GDP data will be followed up on Friday with retail sales data. -------------------------(SPREADS)------------------------------
